description: StreamData model. Defines the abstract Archive base, RawArchive (instant measurements), RollupArchive (derived bucketed-aggregation archives), TimeRangeArchive (externally pre-aggregated [from, to) windowed data), and supporting enum/record types. 1.1.0 → 1.2.0 renamed CkArchive → Archive (abstract) + introduced RawArchive; 1.2.0 → 1.3.0 adds TimeRangeArchive (additive, no entity migration needed); 1.3.0 → 1.4.0 adds RollupArchive.BucketAlignment + the BucketAlignment enum so monthly / weekly / yearly rollups are expressible (additive, pre-1.4.0 entities resolve to FixedSize); 1.4.0 → 1.5.0 adds computed columns on CkArchiveColumn (Name + Formula + ResultType + ComputedState) and the CkComputedColumnResultType / CkComputedColumnState enums (additive, pre-1.5.0 columns have null computed fields); 1.5.0 → 1.6.0 adds the optimistic recompute model (AB#4184): Archive dirty-tracking + observability attributes (DirtyWindows, PendingRecomputeRanges, RecomputeInProgress, Last* fields, all runtime-state), the CkArchiveDirtyWindow / CkArchiveRecomputeRange records, the RecomputeJob history entity, and the CkRecomputeChangeKind / CkRecomputeChangeSource / CkRecomputeJobState / CkRecomputeTrigger enums (additive, pre-1.6.0 entities have null/empty recompute state); 1.6.0 → 1.6.1 adds CkArchiveColumn.ComputedVersion (AB#4189 Phase 7) — the engine-managed physical-column version pointer that lets a computed column's formula change on an active archive via a versioned physical column ({base}__v{N}) + atomic pointer flip, and marks CkArchiveColumn.ComputedState runtime-state too (additive, pre-1.6.1 computed columns are version 0); 1.6.1 → 1.6.2 adds CkArchiveColumn.PendingFormula (AB#4189 Phase 7) — the transient in-progress marker for a formula change that drives the ingest dual-write and is cleared on the atomic swap (additive, null in steady state); 1.6.2 → 1.6.3 widens RollupArchive.BucketSizeMs and RollupArchive.WatermarkLagMs from Int32 to Int64 (AB#4281) so calendar-month (2,419,200,000 ms) and calendar-year (31,536,000,000 ms) bucket widths — which exceed Int32.MaxValue ≈ 24.85 days — persist as numbers instead of being coerced to strings on ImportRt (additive value-type widening; existing Int32 values still load as Int64, no data migration required); 1.6.3 → 1.6.4 adds RollupArchive.ReferenceTimeZone (AB#4290) — an optional IANA time-zone id that makes calendar (day/week/month/year) bucket boundaries DST-correct in a reference zone instead of UTC; used by the resolution-aware series resolver's grain probe (additive, null keeps the pre-1.6.4 UTC behaviour, no data migration required); 1.6.4 → 1.6.5 adds the TimeWeightedAvg value to CkRollupFunction and RollupArchive.CarryLookbackMs (AB#4336) — time-weighted (LOCF) aggregation for event-based archives, stored as an integral/covered-duration column pair; CarryLookbackMs bounds the per-bucket carry-in scan (additive, null falls back to the 35-day engine default, no data migration required); 1.6.5 → 1.6.6 adds the StateDuration value to CkRollupFunction and CkRollupAggregation.ComparisonValue (AB#4336) — absolute time-in-state per bucket for event-based signals, materialised as a single BIGINT milliseconds column with the same LOCF carry as TimeWeightedAvg (additive, ComparisonValue null on existing aggregations, no data migration required); 1.6.6 → 1.6.7 adds the First and Last values to CkRollupFunction (AB#4188) — first/last observed value per bucket (arg_min / arg_max over time), each materialised as a single DOUBLE PRECISION column; chained rollups pick the child bucket with the smallest / largest window boundary and numeric source columns are required (additive, no data migration required); 1.6.7 → 1.6.8 adds Archive.MaxRetroactiveReachMs (AB#4196) — the optional per-archive bounded-retro-reach cap that limits how far before the consumed watermark a single late write may drag an AUTOMATIC dependent recompute (manual recomputeArchive / rewindRollupWatermark stay unbounded); combined with the host StreamData:Recompute:MaxRetroactiveReachHardLimitMs ceiling as the effective cap (additive, null keeps the pre-1.6.8 unbounded behaviour, no data migration required); 1.6.8 → 1.7.0 marks Archive.Status as runtime-state (AB#4582) so a blueprint re-apply (InstallBlueprint -f) preserves the live archive lifecycle status via BlueprintService.PreserveRuntimeStateAttributesAsync instead of overwriting an activated archive with the seeded Disabled value and silently breaking stream-data queries (MINOR bump: flipping an attribute to isRuntimeState is a structural change per the CK SemVer validator, so it requires ≥ 1.7.0 over the published 1.6.8 rather than a PATCH; metadata-only, no data migration required; a fresh install still seeds Disabled and ActivateArchive activates as before); 1.7.0 → 1.7.1 carries no model content change — it is a re-import trigger (AB#4589) so tenants already on 1.7.0 re-import and re-persist the isRuntimeState attribute flags after the octo-construction-kit-engine-mongodb fix that makes CkAttribute.isRuntimeState round-trip through MongoDB (before that fix the flag was dropped on import, the runtime cache read isRuntimeState=false, and the runtime-state preservation never fired; ImportCkModelAsync short-circuits on an already-installed version, so a bump is required to re-import existing tenants). 1.7.1 → 1.8.0 adds multi-source rollup archives (AB#5157): the CkRollupSourceReference record (SourceArchiveRtId plus the optional half-open validity span ValidFrom inclusive / ValidTo exclusive) and RollupArchive.Sources, a RecordArray of those references that becomes the default way to declare a rollup's sources, so history imported at a coarser granularity and data ingested natively at a finer granularity end up in one continuous rollup ladder; RollupArchive.SourceArchiveRtId becomes optional and is deprecated in its description (the CK model has no deprecation flag) — a set value is normalised on read into one unbounded source when Sources is empty, and the platform never writes it any more; BucketAlignment gains the CalendarQuarter value (key 5) for rollups bucketed by calendar quarter in the rollup's reference time zone. MINOR bump: flipping the required SourceArchiveRtId to optional is a structural change the CK SemVer validator rates as Minor, and the new record, attribute and enum value are additive; no data migration is required — rollups stored in the old form keep working unchanged. 1.8.0 → 1.9.0 adds per-range recompute attempt tracking to CkArchiveRecomputeRange (AB#5189): Attempts, NextAttemptAt and LastError, so an obligation that keeps failing backs off and is finally parked instead of being retried every tick forever, and an operator can see which part of a partially recomputed range is stuck and why; and RecomputeJob.LastProgressAt, the heartbeat that lets the drain recognise a job whose process died and continue with its queued work. MINOR bump: the four attributes are additive and default to 0 / null / null / null, so ranges enqueued before the upgrade simply start at attempt zero and older jobs carry no heartbeat; no data migration is required. 1.9.0 → 1.10.0 marks RollupArchive.LastAggregatedBucketEnd and RollupArchive.FrozenUntil as runtime-state (AB#5232): both are written exclusively by the rollup orchestrator and never declared in blueprint seeds, so a blueprint re-apply (InstallBlueprint -f) or plain ImportRt -r used to reset the watermark to null — after which the orchestrator skipped the rollup forever ('watermark is null … Skipping until set') — and clearing FrozenUntil would have allowed recomputing over a truncated source range; paired with the engine-side fix that makes the Upsert preservation inject an existing runtime-state value when the import model omits the attribute (the seed shape for both fields). MINOR bump: flipping an attribute to isRuntimeState is a structural change per the CK SemVer validator, as with 1.7.0; metadata-only, no data migration required. 1.12.0 → 1.13.0 adds opt-in conflict resolution for archive writes: Archive.ConflictPrecedence, the CkArchiveConflictKey record and the CkConflictKeyOrder enum. Every archive write is an upsert on the row key (raw: timestamp + rtid + ckTypeId; windowed: window_start + window_end + rtid + ckTypeId), and until now the update was unconditional, so a re-delivered or out-of-order data point silently replaced newer stored values with older ones — the stored value reflected ARRIVAL order, not the data. ConflictPrecedence declares an ordered list of keys, each naming one of the archive's own columns plus which direction of it counts as better (HigherWins for timestamps and sequence numbers, LowerWins for rank-like codes numbered best-first); competing writes are compared lexicographically, first key dominant, and the better one survives. Because that is a total order over the data itself, the outcome is the same whichever write lands first — delivery order stops mattering rather than merely being satisfied, which is what lets a producer stop pre-sorting its input. Writes that are equal in every key are not ordered by it; the later write replaces the stored row. A single-column form of this (Archive.ConflictVersionColumn, one comparable column, newest wins) was tried first and superseded before publication: a full replay of a productive energy tenant showed it is not enough, because a later ESTIMATE then overwrites an earlier MEASUREMENT — 22 of 805 days came out wrong, and with billing counting measured intervals only, such a day bills as zero. Two keys express the rule correctly ([{DataQuality, LowerWins}, {SourceDocumentDate, HigherWins}]), and generalising to a list rather than hard-coding quality keeps the mechanism usable for any domain that ranks its data. MINOR bump against 1.12.0: the attribute, record and enum are additive and optional, and an empty list preserves the pre-1.13.0 last-write-wins behaviour exactly, so no data migration is required and no existing archive changes behaviour until it opts in. 1.13.0 → 1.13.1 is a PATCH that corrects descriptions only: 1.13.0 said that of two writes equal in every key the row stored first stays, while the storage layer lets the later write replace it (the last key admits equality, so an identical re-delivery stays an idempotent upsert). No type, attribute or behaviour changes. 1.16.0 → 1.17.0 raises the System floor to 2.5 (AB#5528, SECRET attribute value type): 1.16.0 pins System 2.4.0, which an engine that ships System 2.5.0 does not load, so System.StreamData was missing from the CK cache. MINOR bump (dependency version changed); no type, attribute or behaviour changes, no data migration. Loaded only when StreamData is enabled at the instance level.
